text.div:
SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD

  • Otolaryngology consultation with a same-day comprehensive audiologic evaluation: pure-tone air and bone conduction, speech audiometry with word recognition, tympanometry, and acoustic reflexes
  • Tests for treatable causes at intake: blood count, thyroid function, HbA1c, and treponemal antibody; no head imaging for the tinnitus alone
  • MRI of the internal auditory canals with gadolinium to exclude a retrocochlear cause of the asymmetric loss
  • Bilateral prescription hearing aids with real-ear verification, a music program, a tinnitus sound generator, and a remote microphone, with audiology follow-up after fitting
  • Tinnitus education, sound enrichment at night, and cognitive behavioral therapy with a psychologist for tinnitus distress and adjustment; no medication or supplements for tinnitus
  • Depression monitoring with the PHQ-9 at each visit, a structured safety assessment with a written safety plan and the 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline (text and chat), and safety review at every visit
  • Communication access on his terms: his communication preferences on the chart, written summaries, captioning and speech-to-text, workplace accommodation when he chooses to ask, hearing loss peer support, and an introduction to the Deaf community and American Sign Language if he wishes
  • Hearing protection: custom musicians' earplugs for loud rehearsals and limits on unprotected loud sound
  • Repeat audiogram at six months and with any change; same-week assessment for any sudden drop in hearing

resource.title: Ludwig van Beethoven synthetic care plan
resource.description: Primary care for a 30-year-old professional musician with progressive, asymmetric bilateral sensorineural hearing loss and persistent bothersome tinnitus: a targeted history and examination with tuning forks, a comprehensive audiologic evaluation with word recognition, a search for treatable causes and an MRI for the asymmetry, hearing aids and assistive listening fitted for a musician, sound therapy and cognitive behavioral therapy for tinnitus rather than medication, hearing protection, communication access and workplace accommodation, telling cerumen impaction apart from sudden sensorineural loss, and screening for the depression and isolation that hearing loss can bring, with a structured safety assessment and the 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline. Deafness is presented as a change in how he communicates and works, not only as a loss, with Deaf community resources offered on his terms. Built on the AAO-HNS tinnitus, age-related hearing loss, sudden hearing loss, and cerumen guidelines and the CMID depression monograph.
